# SpaNorm {.unnumbered .unlisted}

<p class="tagline">Spatially aware library size normalisation for spatial transcriptomics, in R and Python.</p>

::: {.cta}
[Get started](get-started.qmd){.primary}
[R reference](reference/r/index.html)
[Python reference](reference/python/index.html)
[GitHub](https://github.com/BhuvaLab/SpaNorm)
:::
:::
:::
:::

::: {.intro}
SpaNorm is a spatially aware library size normalisation method that removes library size effects from spatial molecular data while retaining biology. Standard single-cell inspired normalisation is not appropriate for spatial data, because library size is confounded with biology across space [@Bhuva2024; @Atta2023]. SpaNorm models gene- and location-specific effects with smooth thin plate spline functions and keeps only the variation unrelated to library size.
:::

::: {.feature-row}
::: {.card-sn}
### Spatially aware
Gene- and location-specific effects are modelled with smooth thin plate spline functions, so only variation unrelated to library size is removed and biology is kept.
:::
::: {.card-sn}
### R and Python
The R package **SpaNorm** (Bioconductor) and the Python package **spanormpy** (on `AnnData`) share the same method and the same documentation, with R | Python tabs throughout.
:::
::: {.card-sn}
### Built to scale
Parallel workers, block-wise processing of disk-backed counts (R) and an optional GPU backend, with up to 2.7x faster `spanorm` on one H100 MIG slice ([benchmark](get-started.qmd#scaling-to-large-datasets)).
:::
:::

## Install {.section-title}

::: {.card-sn .install-card}

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```r
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")

# release version
BiocManager::install("SpaNorm")
# development version from GitHub
BiocManager::install("BhuvaLab/SpaNorm")
```

## Python

```bash
pip install spanormpy
pip install git+https://github.com/BhuvaLab/spanormpy   # development version
```

For a GPU, install the CUDA build of PyTorch first (see <https://pytorch.org>), then use `backend="gpu"` or the default `backend="auto"`. Optional extras: `pip install "spanormpy[spatial]"` for `SpatialData` input.

:::

:::

## How it works {.section-title}

::: {.figure-card}
![The SpaNorm workflow: SpaNorm takes gene expression and spatial coordinates as inputs. Using a gene-wise model (e.g., Negative Binomial), it decomposes spatially smooth variation into library size independent (biology) and library size related components. The adjusted data keep only the variation unrelated to library size.](SpaNormWorkflow.png){fig-alt="Diagram of the SpaNorm workflow"}
:::

Code examples throughout the site appear in **R | Python** tabs. Choosing a language in one tab switches every tab on the site, and the choice is remembered. See [R vs Python](r-vs-python.qmd) for the name map and the intentional differences.

### Authors

#### SpaNorm (R)

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
# Authors of the R package, generated from Authors@R in ../DESCRIPTION (never hand-written).
# The maintainer (role "cre") also gets a mailto link; ORCID icons only where an ORCID is recorded.
d <- read.dcf("../DESCRIPTION", fields = "Authors@R")
people <- eval(parse(text = d[1, "Authors@R"]))
role_label <- function(p) {
  r <- p$role
  if ("cre" %in% r && "aut" %in% r) "author and maintainer"
  else if ("cre" %in% r) "maintainer"
  else if ("aut" %in% r) "author"
  else paste(r, collapse = ", ")
}
for (p in people) {
  orcid <- unname(p$comment["ORCID"])
  line <- sprintf("- %s, %s", paste(p$given, p$family), role_label(p))
  if (length(orcid) == 1 && !is.na(orcid) && nzchar(orcid)) {
    line <- sprintf('%s [![ORCID](https://orcid.org/assets/vectors/orcid.logo.icon.svg){.orcid fig-alt="ORCID"}](https://orcid.org/%s)',
                    line, orcid)
  }
  if ("cre" %in% p$role && length(p$email) == 1) {
    line <- sprintf("%s ([%s](mailto:%s))", line, p$email, p$email)
  }
  cat(line, "\n", sep = "")
}
```
